_comment: The replay protocol for 08-failure-modes, written before any guard code. It is frozen by hash in data/FROZEN.json together with the guard code and every input file; python/replay.py refuses to run on the test or cross-check set if any of them changed. No model is called anywhere in this demo: every decision replayed here was made by a model in an earlier demo's saved run.
question: If the guards that Articles #23-#29 recommended had been in place, which of the recorded model decisions would they have stopped, which correct work would they have stopped too, and which failures would have passed every one of them?
not_a_blind_test: The guards implement patterns that earlier articles proposed after reading these same runs, and the author had read parts of the runs before writing this protocol. The freeze protects against tuning the guards, thresholds, and patterns to the test results after running them on the test set. It does not make the test blind.

dev.files: results-check.jsonl of 01-05 (the small check runs each demo made before its measured run)
dev.use: Developing and debugging the guard code and the reply patterns. These conversations have no hand labels, so nothing can be tuned to outcomes.

files.04-agent-memory: python/results-qwen2.5_3b.jsonl, designs N, T, S, K

test.run_once: After the freeze, replay.py is run on the test set once. Any change after that is reported as a deviation, with the result before and after.

crosscheck.use: #29's hard checks (owned, amount_valid, amount_available) ran in that loop before any refund. The guards here are compared with them call by call on the same issue_refund calls.

excluded.02-agentic-workflows W and H: Their tool calls were made by code (fixed workflows). H's agent never ran: the router never chose 'other'.
excluded.05-planning W: A developer-written plan; its calls were not model decisions.
excluded.06-state-and-workflows S: The state machine: refund and verification calls made by code. It is #28's version of the patterns, not a subject for them.
excluded.06-state-and-workflows crash runs: Two processes per conversation; the duplicate-after-crash lesson is #28's and is covered there.
excluded.07-human-in-the-loop branch phase: Continuations after scripted reviewer decisions, not new agent decisions about what to request.
excluded.ai-engineering-examples/tool-calling (#8: Excluded by decision (2026-11-24): one repository, and its send_email data is not used.

definitions.agent: Who made a call. 03-multi-agent: the recorded role (agent, manager, specialist:billing, specialist:help_center, drafter, reviewer). Every other demo: one agent per conversation (05's 'plan N' and 'response N' sources and 06's 'first' and 'resume' phases are the same agent).
definitions.agent_tools: ask_billing_specialist and ask_help_center_specialist: calls from one agent to another. Every other tool is a data tool.
definitions.write_tools: issue_refund, hand_off_to_billing, remove_plan_seat. A write is 'executed' when its recorded executed flag is true.
definitions.successful_result: The result of a data-tool call whose recorded 'executed' flag is true. Error results never count, because an error message can repeat the invalid value back.
definitions.request: The customer's message: the question text (01-04), the task question (05), or the scenario message (06, 07).
definitions.app_context: Text the application itself put in the model's context besides the request and the system prompt: 04-agent-memory's memory block for the conversation's design and seed (matched by memory_sha256). None of the other demos' prompts contain an invoice or payment id (checked with grep on 2026-11-24; 05's only id is in W's developer plan, which is excluded). Tool descriptions are deliberately not a source: 01's 'for example INV-0000' is exactly the value the model copied.
definitions.id_arguments: Arguments named invoice_id or payment_id whose value is a string. Values are compared after stripping surrounding whitespace, as the demos' tools do.
definitions.canonical_call: (agent, tool, the parsed arguments serialised as JSON with sorted keys). A call whose arguments are not valid JSON is never canonical-equal to another.

baseline.contract: Every demo already validated each call against its tool's schema (unknown tool, invalid JSON, missing or unknown arguments, wrong types) and sent the error back to the model. That check is not re-implemented: the recorded 'valid' flag is its verdict, and the recorded run shows what the model did next. The new guards below are added on top of it.
baseline.recorded_after_error: For every call with an error result (valid false, or executed false), the next call by the same agent is classified from the record as: identical (same canonical call), same tool with different arguments, a different tool, or none (the agent wrote its reply or the run ended). This is what the models actually did after an error in the original runs; it is not a counterfactual.

budget.applies_to: Every requested tool call, valid or not, by any agent in the conversation.
budget.fires_when: The call is the (K+1)-th tool call requested in the conversation.
budget.why_8: Chosen before the test run: the largest per-conversation model-call budget any of the replayed designs used (05-planning: 8 model calls). A sweep over K is reported separately and does not change the frozen K.

provenance.applies_to: Calls with at least one id argument.
provenance.fires_when: An id argument's value is not one whole token of: the request, the app_context, or a successful_result earlier in the same conversation (from any agent). Tokens are maximal runs of letters, digits, '_' and '-'.

id_format.applies_to: Calls with at least one id argument.
id_format.fires_when: An invoice_id does not match ^INV-[0-9]{4}$, or a payment_id does not match ^PAY-[0-9]{4}$.
id_format.role: A cheaper alternative to provenance. Evaluated independently only; it is not in the sequential order.

repeat.fires_when: The same agent already made the same canonical_call and it produced a successful_result, and no write was executed in the conversation since then.

refund_policy.applies_to: issue_refund(payment_id) in 06-state-and-workflows (the only replayed demo where the model's refund calls reach a payment service). 07's issue_refund has a different policy and its own hard checks; it is the cross-check, not a subject.
rules_in_order: exists: the payment exists in the ledger and belongs to the signed-in customer
is_charge: it is a charge, not a refund
not_refunded: no refund in the ledger refunds it
is_extra_charge: its invoice still has at least two succeeded charges not covered by refunds (a duplicate that hasn't been corrected)
one_per_conversation: no refund was executed earlier in this conversation
refund_policy.ledger: 06's account.json payments, plus the scenario's prior_refunds, plus refunds executed earlier in this conversation (read from their recorded results).
refund_policy.does_not_check: Which month or invoice the customer meant. That is a judgment about the request, not a fact in the data.

handoff_evidence.applies_to: Each specialist reply a manager receives in 03-multi-agent M (the result of an ask_* call).
handoff_evidence.fires_when: The specialist's data calls since its previous reply include no successful_result (either it made no data call, or every one failed).
handoff_evidence.pattern: The reply would be returned as a typed status ('lookup_failed' or 'no_lookup') instead of free text the manager has to interpret.

empty_reply.fires_when: The final reply is empty after stripping whitespace.

tool_call_text.fires_when: The final reply contains a tool call written as text: a JSON object with a "name" key followed by an "arguments" or "parameters" key, or a <tool_call> tag.

unbacked_claim.fires_when: The final reply claims, in the first person or about 'your refund', that a refund or account change was completed, and no write was executed in the conversation.
unbacked_claim.patterns: Fixed in python/guards.py (CLAIM_PATTERNS) during development on the dev set, frozen by hash. Announcements of future actions ('I will now issue a refund') are not completed-action claims and are out of scope for this check.

no_evidence.fires_when: The conversation has no successful_result from any agent and no app_context.

sequential_order._comment: The first-fire replay. The conversation is walked in recorded order; the first guard that fires ends the run (fail closed): the call is not executed and the reply is not sent. What the model would have done if told about the block cannot be replayed, so 'fail closed' is the only policy this replay can evaluate.
per_call: (baseline contract: recorded; an invalid call's error went back to the model and the recorded run continues)

objective._comment: Computed by code from data files and recorded fields, with no judgment.
objective.id_status: For each id argument value: 'owned' if it is an id of the argument's kind (invoice or payment) belonging to customer C-1001 in that demo's account.json, the scenario's prior_refunds, or the refunds recorded as created in that conversation; 'other_customer' if it is such an id belonging to another customer; 'nonexistent' otherwise.
objective.repeat_status: For a call the repeat guard fires on: 'redundant' if its recorded result_text is byte-identical to the earlier successful call's, 'informative' otherwise.
objective.recorded_validity: The recorded valid and executed flags.
objective.refund_action: 06's frozen rule (06-state-and-workflows/data/evaluation.json 'action'): an executed refund is 'wrong' if the charge is not in the scenario's refund_one_of or it is not the conversation's first refund; otherwise 'right'. A refund call that did not execute had no effect ('no_effect').

hand._comment: Hand labels made for the original articles, read from each demo's labels.json and used as they are. Nothing is relabelled here.
hand.answer: 01-05 and 07: the reply's answer label (correct, incorrect, no_answer), matched by the SHA-256 of the exact reply. A label whose hash doesn't match is treated as missing and reported.
hand.06_success: 06: #28's frozen success (06-state-and-workflows/data/evaluation.json 'outcome'), computed exactly as 06's report.py does from the ledger (objective) and the hand-labelled claim and false_statement.
hand.action_claim: 05: fabricated_action. 06: claim is refunded_now and no refund was executed. 07: false_claim.
hand.handoff_facts: 03 M: handoff_labels.json 'replies', per fact present, misstated, or absent. A reply 'carried evidence' if at least one fact is present.

ground_truth.replay_derived: Every guard verdict and every sequential outcome. These are judgments made by this demo's code about recorded decisions, not observations of a system that ran with the guards.

reporting.independent: Each guard evaluated on every call or reply it applies to, as if it were the only new guard, given the recorded history. Reported as counts with their denominators, against the ground truth that fits it.
reporting.sequential: Each conversation's outcome under the sequential_order: stopped at a call (by which guard), reply withheld (by which check), or delivered; crossed with its label. Conversations where a write had already executed before the stop are counted.
reporting.units: Calls, replies, and conversations are counted separately and every row says which.
reporting.rates: Shown only next to their counts and denominators.
reporting.the_limitation: The replay cannot establish how the model would recover after a guard blocks it. A stopped run is reported as stopped, not as fixed.
